sections.title: Writing and conventions · required gap check
sections.passage: A student created a portfolio about how travel and communication changed societies. She began with a research question rather than a list of famous people: How did networks connect communities, and whose experiences were left out of the usual accounts? She compared a map, a trade-route reading, and a translated historical account. Her notes separated quotations, paraphrases, and her own interpretations. When two accounts disagreed, she recorded their authors, purposes, and contexts instead of choosing the more dramatic version. The final presentation used a timeline but did not imply that every change happened everywhere at once. It included an argument supported by evidence and a section explaining limitations. The student concluded that a strong portfolio shows not only a polished product but also how the researcher checked and revised the work.

W4 background: It selects events and scales, leaving out many experiences and connections. Evidence-based argument, source comparison, connections, and reflection. This is an assessment background note written for this packet, not an actual historical primary-source quotation.
